title: 05 Quadratic functions and equations: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 05 Quadratic functions and equations: Visual Guide

1. From Factors To Vertex | two draggable roots driving the factored, expanded and vertex forms at once, with the parabola, its axis of symmetry and its vertex redrawn live | the vertex sits at the midpoint of the roots, so factoring — already taught — hands you h = (r1 + r2)/2 and k for free, and the factor (x + 2) always contributes the root -2

2. Reading Vertex Form | sliders for a, h and k in y = a(x - h)^2 + k, with the direction of opening, the vertex, the axis of symmetry, the extreme value and the count of x-axis crossings all read off the picture | (x - h)^2 is never negative, so the sign of a decides upward or downward and whether k is a minimum or a maximum, while a plus sign inside the bracket means a negative h

3. Completing The Square | an area diagram of x^2 + bx with the missing corner square (b/2)^2 drawn to scale, plus the live five-step solve and a badge naming the quickest method | completing the square rewrites one side as a perfect square plus a constant, which is why it works on every quadratic — and why no linear term means take square roots while integer roots mean factor

4. The Discriminant Dial | a, b and c dragged while the quadratic formula fills itself in and the parabola crosses the x-axis twice, touches once, then misses entirely | b^2 - 4ac counts the solutions before you find them, and because the vertex height is -(b^2 - 4ac)/(4a) a zero discriminant is exactly the case where the turning point sits on the axis

5. Reject The Root | a projectile-height and a revenue model sharing one downward parabola, with the negative-input region shaded and each zero tagged kept or rejected | in an applied quadratic the vertex is the maximum output of interest and the zeros are where the quantity equals 0, but a solution outside the real-world domain is rejected on context rather than negated or rounded
